details:
This update for python-PyJWT fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-101917: attacker traffic can amplify outbound requests to the configured JWKS endpoint (bsc#1283060).
- CVE-2026-101918: unauthenticated request can raise an exception that may produce an HTTP 500 response (bsc#1283061).
- CVE-2026-102267: forwarded credentials may be disclosed or verification keys may be substituted (bsc#1283064).
- CVE-2026-102268: an attacker who knows the public key can forge authenticated HMAC tokens (bsc#1283065).
- CVE-2026-102269: raw-token revocation checks can fail to recognize an equivalent modified token (bsc#1283066).
- CVE-2026-102270: an attacker can cause intensive CPU consumption (bsc#1283067).
- CVE-2026-102271: an attacker who knows the public key can forge authenticated HMAC tokens (bsc#1283068).
- CVE-2026-102274: Malformed RSA JWK aborts parsing of an entire JWK Set (bsc#1283071).
- CVE-2026-102275: an attacker may use a stolen sender-constrained token without the legitimate private key
  (bsc#1283072).
- CVE-2026-103001: reused mutable options mapping can cause verification checks bypass on subsequent decode calls
  (bsc#1283829).

package.name: python-PyJWT
package.ecosystem: SUSE:Linux Enterprise Server for SAP applications 16.0
